season_storylines: Seattle won Super Bowl LX 29-13 over New England behind a dominant defense, then lost OC Klint Kubiak to the Raiders HC job and let Kenneth Walker III walk to Kansas City, so champ-offense continuity is a real question even at a 10.5 win total.

The coaching carousel reshaped half the league: Stefanski to Atlanta, Monken to Cleveland, Kubiak to Las Vegas, Saleh with OC Brian Daboll in Tennessee, Mike McCarthy in Pittsburgh, Jesse Minter with first-time playcaller Declan Doyle in Baltimore, and Mike McDaniel now calling the Chargers offense, which moves TD equity toward LAC, LV and PIT skill players.

Josh Jacobs faces open battery and domestic-abuse charges in Green Bay with a baseline six-game suspension in play under the conduct policy, putting the entire Packers backfield in ambiguity until the legal timeline clears (verify).

Malik Nabers needed a second knee procedure to clean up scar tissue from his Week 4 2025 ACL tear and is now questionable for Week 1, a bigger downgrade in this non-PPR league where his catch-volume floor counts for nothing.

The WR map was redrawn by trades and exits: DJ Moore to Buffalo for a second-round pick, Jaylen Waddle to Denver for the 30th overall pick, and Mike Evans out of Tampa Bay, which hands Emeka Egbuka an alpha target role and TD equity at age 23.

Atlanta's QB battle between Tua Tagovailoa, already missing camp time with a back flare-up, and Michael Penix Jr., not yet cleared from his Week 11 2025 ACL tear, plus Kevin Stefanski's run-heavy history makes Bijan Robinson a volume-and-TD monster while capping every Falcons pass catcher.

Betting markets set Baltimore and the Rams at a league-high 11.5 wins while Arizona sits at a league-low 3.5 with Miami at 4.5, so DST streams against ARI and MIA and yardage-based fades of their skill players are live all season.

Aaron Rodgers declared zero debate that 2026 is his final season, reuniting with Mike McCarthy in Pittsburgh; his low-INT profile plays up at -2 per pick and 6-point passing TDs, with DK Metcalf the direct beneficiary.

Tight end injuries are moving boards: George Kittle says he is ahead of schedule from his January Achilles tear and targeting Week 1, while Sam LaPorta is coming off back microdiscectomy surgery with re-injury risk that pushes targets to Jameson Williams and Jahmyr Gibbs.
Rashee Rice completed his 30-day jail term in May and no NFL suspension is expected, removing the legal discount from his price even as he works back from knee surgery (verify).

teams.outlook: New OC Mike LaFleur brings the McVay system with Marvin Harrison Jr. in the timing-route Adams role, but a league-low 3.5 win total and the league's lowest implied team total cap everyone, and rookie Jeremiyah Love plus Tyler Allgeier are taking first-team reps over an absent James Conner (verify).

Kevin Stefanski installs a run-first scheme while Tua Tagovailoa (back flare-up) and Michael Penix Jr. (ACL rehab, not cleared) fight for QB1, so Bijan Robinson soaks volume and goal-line work while the passing game is a fade until the job settles.

New HC Jesse Minter handed the offense to first-time playcaller Declan Doyle, and with Tyler Linderbaum gone and Mark Andrews declining, Lamar Jackson's rushing keeps his ceiling elite at a league-high 11.5 win total even if passing efficiency dips.

Buffalo paid a second-rounder for a 29-year-old DJ Moore whose YPRR has slid three straight years into a Joe Brady offense that ranked 28th in pass attempts, so Josh Allen's rushing and TD equity remain the only rock-solid asset here.

Jonathon Brooks is getting first-team reps over Chuba Hubbard after his ACL redshirt with Dave Canales praising his recovery, while RT Taylor Moton's blood-clot absence and rookie WR Chris Brazzell's 8-week LCL tear thin the supporting cast.

Ben Johnson's second year with 29 percent of targets vacated by DJ Moore and Olamide Zaccheaus sets up a Luther Burden III, Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland target scramble in a rising offense at a 9.5 win total.

Full continuity for Burrow, Chase, Higgins and Chase Brown plus a rebuilt defense with Dexter Lawrence and Boye Mafe (verify) means fewer forced shootouts but a healthier scoring floor at a 10.5 win total.
Todd Monken arrives with his featured-RB, TE-friendly scheme boosting Quinshon Judkins, but rookie WRs KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston dilute targets and a 5.5 win total caps the passing environment.

Javonte Williams returns off an RB11 season built on 1,200 yards and 11 TDs, and while he was dead last in RB YPRR that receiving hole matters little in non-PPR as long as he holds the early-down and goal-line role.

Sean Payton traded the 30th pick for Jaylen Waddle but historically rotates personnel, so Waddle needs route condensation to matter, and Bo Nix carries sophomore-slide chatter despite a 9.5 win total (verify).

Sam LaPorta's back microdiscectomy leaves his availability shaky, pushing targets toward Jameson Williams' deep routes and more Jahmyr Gibbs usage, exactly the profile this yardage-and-TD format rewards.
Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks left, consolidating routes on Christian Watson and Jayden Reed, while Josh Jacobs' open legal case with suspension risk makes the backup RB a priority stash.

C.J. Stroud gets an upgraded line and David Montgomery for goal-line work, but Montgomery is a 29-year-old dead-zone profile, and Jayden Higgins is the ascending TD-scoring WR after Christian Kirk's departure.

Michael Pittman's exit vacates a 21 percent target share, Alec Pierce is coming off ankle surgery, and slot-only Josh Downs matters less in non-PPR, so TE Tyler Warren is the clearest volume-and-TD beneficiary.

Travis Etienne's exit to New Orleans opens a backfield where Bhayshul Tuten's 97th-percentile speed and 5 TDs on 7 rookie red-zone carries give him a goal-line-plus-explosive profile over Chris Rodriguez, who is off a foot procedure.

Kansas City signed Kenneth Walker III to solidify the backfield after his Super Bowl run (verify), Rashee Rice avoided further suspension, and Mahomes at 6 points per passing TD remains a premium even amid efficiency questions.

Mike McDaniel's quick-trigger scheme replaces Greg Roman, projecting Omarion Hampton for heavy touches plus targets and reviving Justin Herbert's high-TD low-INT profile, making Chargers the top scheme-upgrade stack of 2026.

A league-high 11.5 win total keeps the environment elite, but Matthew Stafford at 38 is screaming TD regression off 46 scores, so buy the yardage earners and fade his price in a 6-point passing TD format.

Klint Kubiak brings his Super Bowl-winning run scheme and 12 personnel, a direct boost to Ashton Jeanty's volume and Brock Bowers' routes, though a 5.5 win total means TDs must come from efficiency not pace.

Jeff Hafley and OC Bobby Slowik inherit a post-Tua reset with an unsettled QB room and a 4.5 win total, leaving De'Von Achane's role uncertain and making Dolphins skill players fade-priced yardage bets (verify).
A quiet camp with no coaching upheaval and an 8.5 win total leaves Minnesota's passing-game roles steady and market-priced, with no signal in the last 72 hours that changes valuations (verify).
The Super Bowl LX runner-up carries a 10.5 win total and Drake Maye's market price has risen accordingly, so you are paying full freight for the offense without a scheme change to add new upside.

Tyler Shough closed 2025 with six straight 17-plus point games and adds goal-line rushing, and the Saints surrounded him with Travis Etienne and rookie Jordyn Tyson, while Bryan Bresee's torn ACL guts the DST interior.

Malik Nabers' second knee procedure makes him a Week 1 question, and a new staff leaning multi-TE personnel points to a grindier offense where the Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy backfield carries the TD equity (verify).
Geno Smith starts under Aaron Glenn after leading the NFL with 32 INTs over two seasons, a brutal profile at -2 per pick with a 5.5 win total, so treat Jets pass catchers as talent-only bets.
New OC Sean Mannion is expected to open up middle-of-field passing for Jalen Hurts and DeVonta Smith, and Hurts' goal-line rushing keeps him a top-tier QB in a 6-point passing TD league.
Mike McCarthy takes over with Aaron Rodgers declaring 2026 his final season, a low-INT high-TD pairing that lifts DK Metcalf's scoring equity while Jaylen Warren leads the backfield.
The champs return at 10.5 wins but lost OC Klint Kubiak and Kenneth Walker III, and rookie Jadarian Price's 6.0 YPC explosiveness has camp buzz as the new lead in a proven scoring offense.

George Kittle is ahead of schedule on his Achilles, but Christian McCaffrey is coming off a 450-touch season, Ricky Pearsall's PCL is swollen, Christian Kirk has a calf issue and Jordan James broke a rib, so rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling is earning real first-team run (verify Kirk and Evans additions).

Mike Evans is gone and Baker Mayfield is playing without a new contract, making Emeka Egbuka the clear alpha after four 20-plus point rookie games, with the offense's TD distribution consolidating around him.

Robert Saleh hands the offense to Brian Daboll, whose pass-heavy scheme boosts Cam Ward's year-two arrow with pro-ready rookie Carnell Tate and Elic Ayomanor competing for targets at a modest 6.5 win total.

Jayden Daniels is confirmed fully healthy after an injury-marred 2025, and new OC David Blough adds under-center play-action, so a soft 7.5 win total reads as market skepticism you can exploit on his rushing ceiling.

breakout_watch.name: Omarion Hampton
breakout_watch.why: Mike McDaniel's Chargers scheme projects him top-15 in RB targets on top of lead-back carries, and in non-PPR the yardage-plus-TD workload is the prize with a healthy ankle after his 2025 fracture.

breakout_watch.name: Ashton Jeanty
breakout_watch.why: Klint Kubiak's run-first Raiders scheme and upgraded infrastructure feed the volume that produced a 31.8-point spike game as a rookie, and goal-line ownership makes him a weekly TD threat.

breakout_watch.name: Luther Burden III
breakout_watch.why: 150 vacated Bears targets, a 2.92 YPRR in the Nacua-Chase cohort, and Ben Johnson's play-calling give him yardage-per-touch upside that beats slot compilers in this format.

breakout_watch.name: Emeka Egbuka
breakout_watch.why: Mike Evans' exit makes him Tampa Bay's alpha after four 20-plus point rookie games, and alpha target quality means end-zone looks, not just catches.

breakout_watch.name: Jayden Higgins
breakout_watch.why: Christian Kirk's departure and his 6 rookie TDs at 9.63 RAS size make him the Texans' red-zone WR, pure TD equity in a non-PPR build.

breakout_watch.name: Bhayshul Tuten
breakout_watch.why: Etienne's exit hands him a backfield where he already owned goal-line work with 5 TDs on 7 red-zone rookie attempts plus 97th-percentile speed for long scores.

breakout_watch.name: Justin Herbert
breakout_watch.why: McDaniel's quick-trigger system historically inflates completions into explosive YAC, and Herbert's high-TD low-INT profile is exactly what 6-point passing TDs and -2 INTs pay for.

breakout_watch.name: Tyler Shough
breakout_watch.why: Six straight 17-plus point games to close 2025, effective goal-line rushing, and new weapons Jordyn Tyson and Travis Etienne make him a dirt-cheap QB2 with rushing-TD ceiling.

breakout_watch.name: Jeremiyah Love
breakout_watch.why: The number 3 overall pick is taking first-team reps in Arizona, and the last nine RBs drafted top-12 all finished top-12 as rookies, so volume plus talent can beat a bad team context (verify team situation).

breakout_watch.name: Jadarian Price
breakout_watch.why: 6.0 YPC explosiveness with 13 scrimmage TDs on limited touches, now stepping into the Super Bowl champs' vacated Kenneth Walker role, a yardage-efficiency profile this scoring loves.

breakout_watch.name: Tyler Warren
breakout_watch.why: Pittman's vacated 21 percent target share funnels to the TE who already commanded a 21.2 percent share, and big-slot TDs travel fine in non-PPR.

breakout_watch.name: Jonathon Brooks
breakout_watch.why: First-team camp reps over Chuba Hubbard with Canales publicly endorsing his ACL recovery, and the former top RB pick costs nothing while carrying lead-back TD upside.

breakout_watch.name: Quinshon Judkins
breakout_watch.why: Todd Monken's Browns scheme historically features one RB heavily, and Judkins is that back with goal-line work in a run-tilted game script.

breakout_watch.name: Carnell Tate
breakout_watch.why: Scouts call him the most pro-ready route runner in the class and Daboll's pass-heavy Titans scheme needs a WR1 for Cam Ward, a downfield role rather than a slot-compiler one (verify).

fade_watch.name: Josh Jacobs
fade_watch.why: Open battery and domestic-abuse charges carry a baseline six-game suspension risk, stacked on age 28, 2,109 career touches and a 4.0 YPC decline; the draft price does not reflect the downside (verify legal outcome).

fade_watch.name: Matthew Stafford
fade_watch.why: Age-38 seasons do not repeat 46 TDs, and in a 6-point passing TD league you are paying peak-TD price for the single most regression-exposed stat in football.

fade_watch.name: Christian McCaffrey
fade_watch.why: Coming off a 450-touch season at his age, and the historical post-mega-workload cliff is steep; his receiving cushion also matters less at zero PPR.

fade_watch.name: Malik Nabers
fade_watch.why: A second knee procedure and Week 1 doubt on a cautious Giants timeline, and his target-hog profile is catch-volume value that this non-PPR format does not pay for.

fade_watch.name: DJ Moore
fade_watch.why: YPRR collapsed from 2.31 to 1.24 entering age 29, now in a Bills offense 28th in pass attempts with committee distribution, a possession profile with shrinking TD equity.

fade_watch.name: James Conner
fade_watch.why: Buried behind Jeremiyah Love, Tyler Allgeier and Trey Benson on camp reps and absent from drills, on the team with the league's lowest implied total (verify).

fade_watch.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
fade_watch.why: ADP spiked on Njoku's exit but new rookie WRs Concepcion and Boston dilute targets, he missed offseason work, and defenses now gameplan for him in a 5.5-win offense.

fade_watch.name: David Montgomery
fade_watch.why: Age 29 with opportunities falling three straight years to a career-low 9.1 PPG, now TD-dependent behind a middling Houston line, the classic dead-zone RB.

fade_watch.name: Geno Smith
fade_watch.why: League-most 32 INTs over two seasons is disqualifying at -2 per pick, and a 5.5-win Jets environment offers no TD volume to offset it.

fade_watch.name: Sam LaPorta
fade_watch.why: Back microdiscectomy recovery with re-injury risk in a crowded target tree; pay for the healthy Lions pieces instead.

uncertainty_note: Genuinely unsettled right now: the Atlanta QB1 job (Tua's back versus Penix's ACL clearance), the Josh Jacobs legal and suspension timeline, Malik Nabers' Week 1 availability, Shemar Stewart's imaging results, and several reported 2026 player-team moves (Mike Evans and Christian Kirk in San Francisco, Kenneth Walker to Kansas City, Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier in Arizona) that come from secondhand summaries and should firm up when preseason games start August 6; depth-chart reads from late-July practices can flip within a week.
